headline: SIFT uses pairwise judging and disaggregated search to improve recursive coding-agent benchmarks
summary: A Sep 17, 2026 arXiv preprint introduces SIFT, which uses pairwise LLM judgments and a regularized Bradley–Terry ranking signal to steer a disaggregated search over coding-agent modifications, reserving more expensive task evaluations for selected candidates. The authors report Polyglot gains over named recursive-search baselines and a TerminalBench result where judge-ranked selection outperforms selection by search-subset score across three repeated full evaluations. These are author-reported results from one preprint. A resource table and adjacent prose disagree substantially on the o3-mini/GPT-5.4 run's steps, cost and CPU time, so the paper's efficiency comparison is not resolved here.
